title: Grok reviewer cancelled by a permission prompt: brief it, and fall back to the next row
lead: *Proposed.* A Grok reviewer, gate, architect, UI or spec-check round is told which shell commands run in plan mode without approval. A round the Grok CLI cancelled because a command needed approval no longer stops the run: it ends as an error exit, so the role's next row (Claude) takes the round, unless the final report was already written, in which case the report is kept.
findings_note: Wave 7, 2026-11-04 (slicer s313): the first real Grok reviewer round (grok-4.7 medium, plan mode) ran 3.5 minutes, then tried a multi-statement `python3 -c` that wrote a temp file. stderr: "permission required: Execute ... was not run, as a headless run cannot ask for approval". The CLI cancelled the whole run (result subtype error_during_execution, is_error true, stop_reason cancelled, exit 0), and ork ended it as "reviewer round 1 exited unclassified", which stopped the run. The reviewer had already written its full report; it was lost. Evidence: ~/.local/state/ork/fixtures/grok/20261104T061623Z-1183348939 (cmd, stderr, stdout). Needed: (1) the Grok read-only brief lists the commands that run without approval (git, rg, cat, ls, read-only test runs) and says a command that needs approval ends the run, so do not issue one; (2) an unclassified or cancelled Grok round moves to the next row of the role (Claude) instead of stopping the run, as out_of_credits does; (3) a cancelled round that already produced its final report text keeps that report. Related: S268, S269, S277.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Wave 7 (2026-11-04) and wave 8 (2026-11-05): two Grok reviewer rounds ended "exited unclassified" and the run stopped (slicer s313; ork S278). Both fixtures show the same cause (`~/.local/state/ork/fixtures/grok/20261104T061623Z-1183348939` and `.../20261105T184036Z-1845077106`):

- In plan mode, simple single shell commands ran: `git status --short`, `git diff -- PATH ...`, `git diff --check -- PATH ...`; so did the built-in file tools (read_file, grep, list_dir).
- A compound command was refused: a git status, echo and git diff chain joined with `&&` (first fixture) and a slicer goals, echo and slicer list chain joined with `&&` (second fixture). A `python3 -c '...'` call ended the first run after 3.5 minutes.
- The CLI then cancelled the whole run: stderr "permission required: Execute ... was not run, as a headless run cannot ask for approval", exit code 0, and a final result line with `subtype: error_during_execution`, `is_error: true`, `stop_reason: cancelled`, `errors: ["cancelled"]`. The first run's reviewer had already written its full report; it was lost.

What the code does at HEAD of main (read 2026-11-05): `Run` sets `ExitUnclassified` for any run that exited and did not complete cleanly (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:310-316`), the daemon maps it to `engine.ExitUnclassified` (`internal/daemon/runner.go:165-175`), and `fallbackExit` accepts only rate-limited, out-of-credits and error exits (`internal/engine/ledger.go:45-47`), so an unclassified exit stops the run instead of moving to the next row. The brief prints the claude-style allowlist for read-only roles (`doneWhen`, `internal/engine/brief.go:153-170`), which Grok ignores (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:4`: `--tools` takes tool names, not patterns), so a Grok role is never told its real limit.

Not verified, so not claimed by this slice: whether `rg`, `slicer show` or a test run work alone in plan mode (the fixtures hold no such call). The brief names only the forms the fixtures show running.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/agent/grok/grok_test.go`:

- `TestGrokPermissionCancelIsAnErrorExit`: running the adapter against `08-permission-cancelled` (the stdout above, the stderr above, exit code 0) returns `Exit == ExitError`, no Go error, and a `Reason` that starts with `grok: cancelled on a permission prompt` and names the refused command's first 60 characters. Fails first: the exit is `ExitUnclassified` and the reason is empty.
- `TestGrokPermissionCancelKeepsAFinishedReport`: a stream whose last assistant message with text holds a full report (ending with the heading `## Owner needed` and the word `none`), then a tool call refused, then the cancelled result, with no report file, returns `Exit == ExitOK`, `Report` equal to that message text and `Reason` naming the cancelled command. Fails first: the exit is `ExitUnclassified` and the report is empty.
- `TestGrokPermissionCancelKeepsAReportFileToo`: the same cancel with a `Spec.ReportFile` that holds text returns `ExitOK` and the file text (the file wins over the message, as `TestGrokReportFileTakesPrecedence` at `:295` already says for a clean run). Fails first: the exit is `ExitUnclassified`.
- `TestGrokPermissionCancelWithoutAFinishedReportIsAnErrorExit`: a cancel after an assistant message that holds no `## Owner needed` heading (commentary such as "I will check the diff", or only a tool call) returns `ExitError` and an empty `Report`. Fails first: the exit is `ExitUnclassified`.
- `TestGrokOtherFailuresStayUnclassified`: `TestGrokIncompleteOrFailedStreamIsNotOK`'s cases and `06-bad-model` still return `ExitUnclassified` (a plain error result without `stop_reason: cancelled` is not a permission cancel). Fails first: not applicable; it guards the old behavior and must stay green.

In `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:

- `TestGrokReadOnlyDoneWhenNamesTheFormsThatRun`: for `Vendor: "grok"` and each read-only role the `## Done when` section lists the three verified forms (`git status --short`, `git diff -- PATH`, `git diff --check -- PATH`), the file tools, says one command for each call with no `&&`, `;`, pipe, `echo`, redirect or `python3 -c`, and says a command that needs approval ends the run and loses the report. It does not print the claude-style `Allow` entries. Fails first: it prints the `Allow` entries.
- `TestClaudeAndCodexReadOnlyDoneWhenIsUnchanged`: for `Vendor: "claude"` and `"codex"` the section is byte for byte what it was (the existing S277 tests stay green). Fails first: not applicable; guard.

In `internal/engine/speccheck_test.go`:

- `TestSpecCheckBriefNamesTheRowsVendorLimits`: a spec check whose lineup is a Grok row then a Claude row records the brief each row received (the fake runner keeps its prompt); the Grok row's brief has the Grok `## Done when` text (the three verified forms, no `&&`) and the Claude row's brief has the claude-style `Allow` text. Fails first: both rows get the same brief, built without a vendor.

In `internal/engine/round_test.go`:

- `TestPermissionCancelledGrokReviewerFallsBackToTheNextRow`: a lineup of a Grok reviewer row then a Claude row, the runner returns `ExitError` with the permission-cancel reason for Grok and a valid report for Claude. Expect: the second row runs the same round, the run goes on, and the Grok vendor is not marked out. Fails first: not applicable if `ExitError` already falls back; it pins the mapping and must be green once the adapter test is green.

Re-anchor 2026-11-05: doneWhen at internal/engine/brief.go:159-163 already omits Allow entries for all read-only roles. TestClaudeAndCodexReadOnlyDoneWhenIsUnchanged must pin the existing read-only checklist byte for byte; TestSpecCheckBriefNamesTheRowsVendorLimits expects that unchanged text for Claude, not Allow entries. Grok tests still fail first because its verified command forms are absent. TestGrokReportFileTakesPrecedence remains at internal/agent/grok/grok_test.go:295 and TestGrokIncompleteOrFailedStreamIsNotOK at :307. Add the row-vendor test in internal/engine/speccheck_test.go using specConfig at :99.

Final anchors: adapter tests now begin at grok_test.go:339, :355, :374, :396 and :419; brief tests at brief_test.go:436 and :451; row-vendor test at speccheck_test.go:216; fallback test at round_test.go:47. Harness is internal/engine/harness_test.go:195, not engine_test.go. The Grok brief names && only as a prohibited form, never as an executable compound command example. Guards and the existing fallback test are expected green before product changes, as specified above. Mutation checks strengthened file-only recovery and synchronized the vendor-out clock.

Self-check: TestGrokPermissionCancelWithoutAFinishedReportIsAnErrorExit also covers a later assistant event with an empty text block; it must replace the earlier finished text, unlike a tool-only event. Observed red: exit = ok, want error; unfinished report = "Review\n## Owner needed\nnone". The unclassified guard now begins at grok_test.go:420; Run classification at grok.go:332.

Current round re-anchor: TestClaudeAndCodexReadOnlyDoneWhenIsUnchanged is at brief_test.go:454 and pins literal expected checklists for each role. The Grok restrictions assertion checks the full prohibition sentence. The fallback test fails explicitly if no Claude reviewer report was recorded. Product code and the listed tests were already present when this implementer process started; this process verifies their mutations and does not claim their original test-first failures.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first from the failing list; confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. In `grok.go`, add `StopReason` to `Event`. In the result case, remember a result with `stop_reason == "cancelled"`. After the process ends, a run whose result is cancelled and whose stderr holds `permission required` is a permission cancel: `Exit = ExitError`, `Reason = "grok: cancelled on a permission prompt: " + the command named in stderr, cut at 60 characters`. A stderr without that text stays unclassified.
3. Keep `ExitCode 0` handling as is; do not mark the vendor out (`ExitError` does not, `round.go:405-412`). Do not change the credits, bad-model or auth classification.
4. Owner decision 2026-11-05 (interview in the ork session): a cancelled round keeps its final message as the report. Keep the text of the last complete `assistant` event that has text blocks (not the partial-message deltas). Count it as a finished report only when it contains the line `## Owner needed`, the heading every role report ends with; commentary and tool-call-only messages are not reports. A non-empty report file wins over the message. If a finished report exists, return `ExitOK` with it and keep the cancel `Reason` for the role row; the shape check (`CheckReport`) then judges it as for any other report. Otherwise return `ExitError` with no report. Never return a report with a non-OK exit.
5. In `speccheck.go`, move the `BuildBrief` call into the row loop so each row's brief carries its own `Vendor`; keep the fingerprint, the status check and the report removal before it as they are.
6. In `doneWhen`, for `Vendor == "grok"` and a read-only role, print the three verified forms and the rules above in place of the `Allow` forms; keep the text under the 40-line limit of the section.
7. Do not claim `rg`, `slicer` or test commands work in plan mode. Do not change `Args`, the plan-mode flag or the vendor out marking.
8. Update `docs/design.md` and `docs/how-it-works.md` in the same diff.

sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/agent/grok ./internal/engine -run 'Grok|PermissionCancel|DoneWhen'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: classify the permission cancel as `ExitUnclassified` again; `TestGrokPermissionCancelIsAnErrorExit` goes red. Print the `Allow` entries for Grok; `TestGrokReadOnlyDoneWhenNamesTheFormsThatRun` goes red.
- `rg -n "larder|/Users" testdata/vendors/grok/08-permission-cancelled.stdout` prints nothing.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] With Grok marked back (`ork vendor back grok`), the next wave's first Grok reviewer round either finishes its report or falls to the Claude row, and the run does not stop.
